system_prompt:
You are a principal solution architect at a top-tier consulting firm.

Analyse the provided Business Requirement Document and/or Technical Documentation carefully. Extract EVERYTHING relevant and produce a complete architecture JSON.

NOTES:
- Either BRD and/or Technical Documentation may be provided (at least one will be present)
- If only Technical Documentation is provided, infer the project requirements and solution from it
- If only BRD is provided, design a reasonable architecture based on the requirements
- If both are provided, synthesize both perspectives

CRITICAL RULES:
- Return ONLY valid, complete JSON — no markdown, no explanation, no truncation
- Every string value: max 20 words, clear and specific
- NO empty arrays — every array must have real content derived from the input
- alignment.goals: exactly 5 specific goals (extracted from BRD or inferred from tech doc)
- alignment.success_metrics: exactly 5 measurable KPIs
- problem_statement.current_pain_points: exactly 5-6 specific pains
- proposed_solution.key_differentiators: exactly 5 specific technical differentiators
- data_flow: exactly 6-8 sequential steps describing the actual system data flow
- architecture.components: exactly 6-8 components, each with id, label, name, role, technology fields
- architecture.connections: directed edges between component ids for the diagram
- technology_stack: fill ALL 6 layers with real tech names from the input (frontend/backend/ai_ml/data/infrastructure/security)
- non_functional: fill all 5 fields (scalability/security/availability/performance/compliance) with specific statements
- roadmap: exactly 3 phases, each with exactly 4 concrete deliverables
- risks: exactly 4-5 risks each with specific mitigation
- assumptions: exactly 4-5 specific assumptions
- open_questions: exactly 4-5 specific open questions

IMPORTANT for architecture.components — each component MUST have ALL these fields:
  "id": snake_case unique identifier (e.g. "fastapi_backend")
  "label": short display name (e.g. "FastAPI Backend")
  "name": full descriptive name (e.g. "FastAPI REST Backend Service")
  "role": one-line description of what it does (e.g. "Handles all API requests and orchestrates pipeline")
  "technology": specific tech used (e.g. "FastAPI, Python, Pydantic, Uvicorn")

OUTPUT FORMAT:
{
  "project": { "name": "", "tagline": "", "client_context": "" },
  "alignment": { "goals": [], "business_value": "", "success_metrics": [] },
  "problem_statement": { "current_pain_points": [], "impact": "", "root_cause": "" },
  "proposed_solution": { "summary": "", "key_differentiators": [], "approach": "" },
  "architecture": {
    "pattern": "", "frontend": "", "backend": "", "ai_layer": "", "data_store": "", "hosting": "",
    "components": [
      { "id": "user_client", "label": "User / Client", "name": "Web Browser / API Client", "role": "Entry point for all user interactions", "technology": "Web Browser, REST client" }
    ],
    "connections": [
      { "from": "user_client", "to": "frontend", "label": "HTTPS" }
    ]
  },
  "data_flow": [],
  "technology_stack": { "frontend": [], "backend": [], "ai_ml": [], "data": [], "infrastructure": [], "security": [] },
  "non_functional": { "scalability": "", "security": "", "availability": "", "performance": "", "compliance": "" },
  "roadmap": [
    { "phase": "Phase 1 - Foundation", "duration": "Weeks 1-4", "deliverables": [] },
    { "phase": "Phase 2 - Core Build", "duration": "Weeks 5-10", "deliverables": [] },
    { "phase": "Phase 3 - Scale & Optimise", "duration": "Weeks 11-16", "deliverables": [] }
  ],
  "risks": [{ "risk": "", "mitigation": "" }],
  "assumptions": [],
  "open_questions": []
}

project.name: BI Attribute Overlap Analyser
project.tagline: AI-powered duplicate detection and governance for enterprise Power BI report attributes
project.client_context: Enterprise BI governance team managing report sprawl across large-scale Power BI deployments

goals: Detect duplicate and semantically similar Power BI report attributes to reduce enterprise report sprawl
Enable BI governance workflows with exportable Excel overlap analysis reports
Automate hybrid similarity scoring across uploaded report attribute datasets without manual effort
Support embedding within existing enterprise BI portals with minimal hosting overhead
Accelerate data stewardship decisions by surfacing LLM-confirmed high-confidence attribute overlaps at 0.95 threshold
alignment.business_value: Reduces manual BI audit effort, enforces data governance standards, and eliminates redundant report attributes across the enterprise
success_metrics: 95% reduction in manual attribute comparison time per governance audit cycle
LLM-confirmed overlap detection accuracy above 95% confidence threshold consistently
Excel export generated and downloadable within 30 seconds for datasets up to 1000 attributes
Zero hardcoded credentials incidents post-deployment via secrets management enforcement
Tool successfully embedded in enterprise BI portal with 100% authorised-user access control

current_pain_points: Hardcoded LLM API credentials and endpoint in server.py represent a critical production security vulnerability
TF-IDF vectorizer refitted per request with no caching, causing repeated computation overhead on every upload
LLM parallelism capped at max_workers=2 with only 3 retries, severely limiting throughput under concurrent load
Input model strictly requires Table and Field columns, making tool brittle against non-conforming uploads
No persistence layer means all analysis results are ephemeral with zero historical audit trail
No authentication or authorisation controls on the upload endpoint, exposing governance data to unauthorised access
problem_statement.impact: Governance analysts face security risks, slow processing, and no audit history, undermining enterprise BI rationalisation efforts
problem_statement.root_cause: Prototype-grade implementation lacks production hardening: no secrets management, no caching, no persistence, and no access controls

proposed_solution.summary: Hardened, scalable SPA plus Python backend with Azure Key Vault secrets, TF-IDF caching, async LLM batching, persistent audit store, and enterprise SSO
key_differentiators: Hybrid three-signal similarity pipeline combining TF-IDF cosine, Levenshtein, and Jaccard trigrams for robust attribute matching
Azure-hosted Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct LLM confirmation layer enforcing 0.95 confidence threshold for high-precision overlap flagging
Persisted TF-IDF model artifacts with runtime caching eliminating redundant per-request vectorizer fitting overhead
Azure Key Vault integration replacing all hardcoded credentials with secure, rotatable secret references
Audit trail persistence layer storing all historical overlap analyses for governance reporting and compliance evidence
proposed_solution.approach: Iteratively harden the existing prototype: secure secrets, add caching and persistence, scale LLM concurrency, enforce input validation, and integrate enterprise SSO

architecture.pattern: Static SPA frontend with Python REST backend, Azure AI inference layer, and persistent audit data store
architecture.frontend: Static HTML5 SPA with Bootstrap 5.3.3, drag-and-drop upload, tabbed report cards, and Excel export
architecture.backend: Python server.py exposing /find_overlaps REST endpoint with ThreadPoolExecutor and hybrid similarity pipeline
architecture.ai_layer: Azure-hosted Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct via AzureOpenAI client with batched LLM calls and exponential backoff
architecture.data_store: Persistent audit store for historical overlap analyses; cached TF-IDF model artifacts in memory or blob storage
architecture.hosting: Azure Static Web Apps for frontend; Azure App Service or Container Apps for Python backend

components.label: User / Client
components.name: Enterprise Governance User Browser
components.role: Entry point for BI analysts and data stewards uploading attribute files and reviewing results

components.label: SPA Frontend
components.name: Static Single-Page Application
components.role: Renders drag-and-drop upload, tabbed report cards, filterable tables, and Excel export UI

components.label: API Gateway / Auth
components.name: Azure API Management with SSO Enforcement
components.role: Enforces authentication, authorisation, and rate limiting on all backend API calls
components.technology: Azure API Management, Azure AD, OAuth 2.0, JWT

components.label: Python Backend
components.name: Python REST Backend Service
components.role: Exposes /find_overlaps endpoint, orchestrates similarity pipeline, manages LLM batching and caching
components.technology: Python, FastAPI or Flask, ThreadPoolExecutor, Pydantic, Uvicorn

components.label: Similarity Engine
components.name: Hybrid Similarity Scoring Pipeline
components.role: Computes TF-IDF cosine, Levenshtein edit distance, and Jaccard trigram scores for attribute pairs
components.technology: scikit-learn TF-IDF, python-Levenshtein, custom Jaccard trigram, NumPy

components.label: LLM Service
components.name: Azure Llama-3.3-70B Inference Service
components.role: Confirms high-confidence attribute overlaps above 0.95 threshold via batched LLM prompts

components.label: Secrets Store
components.name: Azure Key Vault Secrets Manager
components.role: Stores and serves LLM API credentials and endpoint URLs securely at runtime
components.technology: Azure Key Vault, Managed Identity, Azure SDK

components.label: Audit Store
components.name: Persistent Audit and Cache Data Store
components.role: Persists historical overlap analysis results and caches fitted TF-IDF model artifacts
components.technology: Azure Blob Storage or Azure SQL, Redis Cache, Python pickle

data_flow: Governance analyst drags and drops Excel or CSV attribute file onto SPA frontend upload interface
SPA sends multipart file upload POST request to /find_overlaps via API Gateway with JWT auth token
API Gateway validates JWT, enforces authorisation policy, and forwards request to Python backend
Python backend validates and sanitises file input, enforcing required Table and Field column schema
Similarity engine computes TF-IDF cosine (45%), Levenshtein (25%), and Jaccard trigram (30%) scores for all attribute pairs using cached vectorizer artifacts
Candidate pairs above similarity threshold are batched in groups of 25 and submitted to Azure Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct with exponential backoff
LLM returns confidence scores; pairs at or above 0.95 threshold are flagged as confirmed high-confidence overlaps
Final overlap results are persisted to audit store and returned as JSON to SPA for tabbed display and Excel export

non_functional.scalability: Backend scales horizontally on Azure Container Apps; LLM concurrency increased beyond max_workers=2 via async batching and queue-based dispatch
non_functional.security: All credentials stored in Azure Key Vault via Managed Identity; file inputs sanitised; endpoints protected by Azure AD OAuth 2.0 JWT enforcement
non_functional.availability: Azure App Service or Container Apps SLA of 99.95%; retry logic with exponential backoff and jitter ensures resilience against LLM rate-limit errors
non_functional.performance: TF-IDF model artifacts cached in Redis eliminating per-request refitting; LLM batches of 25 pairs with backoff sustain sub-30-second response for 1000 attributes
non_functional.compliance: Audit trail of all overlap analyses persisted in Azure SQL for governance evidence; data residency enforced within enterprise Azure tenant boundaries

deliverables: Migrate all hardcoded LLM credentials to Azure Key Vault with Managed Identity integration
Implement file upload input validation and sanitisation enforcing Table and Field schema
Deploy SPA to Azure Static Web Apps and backend to Azure App Service with TLS
Integrate Azure AD OAuth 2.0 JWT authentication on API Gateway for all endpoints
Implement Redis-backed TF-IDF model artifact caching to eliminate per-request vectorizer refitting
Increase LLM concurrency with async batching, configurable worker pool, and exponential backoff with jitter
Build persistent audit store in Azure SQL to record all historical overlap analysis results
Refactor similarity engine into independently testable module with unit test coverage above 80%
Migrate backend to Azure Container Apps with auto-scaling rules based on request queue depth
Add governance dashboard to SPA surfacing historical audit trail with trend and deduplication metrics
Implement configurable similarity threshold and weight tuning UI for governance analysts
Conduct end-to-end performance and penetration testing; remediate all critical and high findings

risks.risk: Azure Llama-3.3-70B rate limits cause unacceptable latency spikes under concurrent governance analyst usage
risks.mitigation: Implement async LLM dispatch queue, increase max_workers, apply exponential backoff with jitter, and evaluate provisioned throughput tier

risks.risk: Non-conforming uploaded files without Table and Field columns cause silent failures or incorrect similarity results
risks.mitigation: Enforce strict server-side schema validation with descriptive error responses and SPA-side pre-upload column mapping UI

risks.risk: Persisted audit data in Azure SQL contains sensitive enterprise attribute metadata requiring data classification controls
risks.mitigation: Apply Azure SQL data masking, row-level security, and encryption at rest; classify audit data under enterprise data governance policy

risks.risk: TF-IDF cache invalidation logic may serve stale model artifacts after vocabulary drift in new uploaded datasets
risks.mitigation: Implement cache key based on dataset vocabulary hash; set TTL policy and provide manual cache flush endpoint for administrators

risks.risk: Embedding tool in enterprise BI portal via iframe or script inclusion may introduce CSP and CORS policy conflicts
risks.mitigation: Define explicit CORS allowlist and Content Security Policy headers; coordinate with BI portal administrator during Phase 1 deployment

assumptions: Enterprise Azure tenant is available with permissions to provision Key Vault, App Service, API Management, and Azure AD app registrations
Uploaded attribute files will consistently contain at minimum Table and Field columns after Phase 1 validation enforcement
Azure Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct endpoint remains available under the 2024-05-01-preview API version throughout the project lifecycle
BI Portal Administrator has authority to embed the SPA and configure CORS and CSP policies within the enterprise portal environment
Governance analysts and data stewards have or can be provisioned Azure AD identities for OAuth 2.0 authentication enforcement
open_questions: What is the maximum expected number of attribute pairs per upload, and what is the acceptable end-to-end response time SLA for governance analysts?
Should the 0.95 LLM confidence threshold be configurable per-tenant or per-session, or remain a fixed system-wide governance standard?
Is there a requirement to integrate the audit trail with existing enterprise data catalogue or governance platforms such as Microsoft Purview?
What data residency and sovereignty requirements apply to attribute data sent to the Azure-hosted Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct inference endpoint?
Will the tool need to support multi-file uploads for cross-report comparison, or is single-file pairwise analysis within one upload sufficient?
